referents.why: 'To them' (autois) after 'was saying': the crowd, plural. No plural candidate is offered.
Interrogative 'What evil' as object of 'did He commit'. Names no referent.
'Him' (auton), object of 'Crucify': Jesus. Not among the candidates. This verse has an empty before window, so Jesus named in Mrk.15.5 and Mrk.15.12 is not offered.
Implied 'he' of 'did He commit': Jesus, the one accused. Not among the candidates (see w14).
Implied 'you' of the command 'Crucify Him' is the one the crowd speaks to: Pilate, the questioner in this verse.

links.why: The question is the object of 'was saying'. Grammar nesting kept beside the content link.
The command is the object of 'shouted'. Grammar nesting kept beside the content link.
R1: 'shouted' introduces what is said, the command.
The connective is Greek de ('but'), and cl2 sets the crowd's shout against Pilate's question. 'And then' does not carry that opposition.
BSB 'But they shouted all the louder': the text says 'but' before cl2, contrasting the shout with Pilate's question.

groups.why: Frame cl0; part is the question cl1; sender is Pilate. The builder's addressee w4 is the crowd, which is not a candidate, so it is omitted.
groups.category: question turn with addressee not in candidates

groups.why: Frame cl2; part the command cl3; addressee Pilate (cl3s). The builder's sender w10 is not a candidate here. The reply is spoken by the crowd (R2, alternation), which is not a candidate, so the sender is omitted.
groups.category: reply turn with sender not in candidates

cant_tell.what: subject 'they' of cl2 (the crowd shouting) and the crowd as addressee of Pilate's question (w4)
cant_tell.why: The crowd is not a candidate, and the subject of cl2 has no slot.

cant_tell.what: Jesus as referent of w14 and cl1s
